If you are dealing with fox activity or an increasing fox population on your property and are looking for professional fox pest control services in Melbourne, you are in the right place.

blocks.label: Intro HTML
blocks.value: Foxes may appear harmless, but their presence can cause serious problems for residential and commercial properties. Below are some of the common issues caused by fox infestations:

metadata.title: Threat to Pets & Livestock
metadata.description: Foxes are natural predators and can attack small pets, poultry, and livestock. This poses serious risks to households, farms, and rural properties.

metadata.title: Property & Structural Damage
metadata.description: Foxes dig dens under houses, sheds, and fences. Their burrowing can weaken foundations, damage gardens, and create safety hazards over time.

metadata.title: Health & Disease Risks
metadata.description: Foxes may carry parasites and diseases that can affect pets and humans. Their presence increases health risks, especially in residential areas.

metadata.title: Environmental & Wildlife Impact
metadata.description: Uncontrolled fox populations harm native wildlife and disrupt local ecosystems, leading to biodiversity loss.

metadata.title: Rapid Population Growth
metadata.description: Foxes reproduce quickly, and once they settle in an area, their population can increase rapidly, making control difficult without professional fox pest control.

metadata.title: Business & Farm Disruptions
metadata.description: For farms and businesses, fox activity can cause livestock losses, property damage, and financial impact, especially in agricultural and semi-urban areas.

blocks.label: Intro HTML
blocks.value: Foxes are intelligent and adaptable animals. Preventing fox infestations requires proactive measures to remove food sources, block access points, and reduce shelter opportunities. Here are some effective ways to keep foxes away from your property:

tips.title: 1. Secure Food Sources
list: Do not leave pet food outdoors overnight
Secure rubbish bins with tight-fitting lids
Clean up fallen fruits and food waste regularly
Avoid feeding wildlife near your property

tips.title: 2. Seal Entry Points
list: Repair gaps under fences and gates
Block access under decks, sheds, and houses
Use wire mesh to seal potential denning areas
Close off crawl spaces and openings

tips.title: 3. Eliminate Shelter & Hiding Spots
list: Clear dense bushes and overgrown vegetation
Remove debris, wood piles, and unused materials
Trim hedges close to the ground
Keep yards open and well-maintained

tips.title: 4. Protect Pets & Livestock
list: Secure poultry coops with strong fencing
Keep small pets indoors at night
Use motion-sensor lights around animal enclosures
Avoid leaving animal carcasses exposed

tips.title: 5. Maintain Clean Outdoor Areas
list: Keep gardens tidy and free of food scraps
Remove standing water sources
Store compost securely to avoid attracting foxes
Maintain regular yard inspections

tips.title: 6. Use Deterrents Where Needed
list: Install motion-activated lights or sprinklers
Use fox deterrent sprays in high-risk areas
Fence off vulnerable zones such as chicken runs
Rotate deterrents to maintain effectiveness

tips.title: 7.Monitor Fox Activity
list: Watch for signs like tracks, droppings, or digging
Act quickly if fox activity increases
Early action helps prevent population growth

items.question: 4. How quickly can fox removal be done in Melbourne?

items.question: 5. How can I prevent foxes from entering my property?
